Foundations: Tensors & Data
Introduction to Tensors
Tensors are multi-dimensional arrays: the fundamental data structure of machine learning.
Inspect One Packet
A tensor is a numeric array with a shape, the size of each axis. A flat list of three readings has shape [3]. TensorFlow
The shape tells you how the readings are arranged. dataSync() returns their values as a typed array; Array.from() copies
A tensor's rank counts its axes: a scalar number has rank 0, a flat vector has rank 1, and a matrix has rank 2. A [2, 3]
Dispose a tensor after its final use. In the example, reading lives until dispose(). The temporary sum lives only inside
A backend is the implementation that runs operations on the CPU or GPU. With the default float32 dtype, the CPU backend
Keeping Repeated Runs Small
Dispose tensors when you finish with them, on every backend. tf.memory().numTensors counts tensors that have not been di
GPU resources need explicit cleanup. CPU values use JavaScript-managed storage, but relying on garbage collection leaves
Use a cleanup scope for temporary tensors and dispose anything you retain:
tf.tidy() runs a synchronous callback and disposes its temporary tensors. Do not pass it an async function. Return a ten
You can try the channel-layout experiment now and return to this challenge. That preview does not mark either lesson com
